SECTION 1  
* A 24-year-old writer named Sam Webb says older people unfairly blame young adults for spending money on things like holidays and meals out, instead of saving for a house—which is extremely hard to afford.  
* He explains that house prices in the UK are rising fast while homes for sale are scarce, and banks are making it harder than ever to get a mortgage.  
* Because of this, many young people feel they’ll never be able to buy a home and will instead spend their lives paying rent to landlords—who then criticize them for not saving enough.  
* Young people under 25 don’t get the higher “national living wage”; those aged 21–24 can legally be paid as little as £7.05/hour, and those 18–20 even less—just £5.60/hour—for the same work.  
* Even with full-time work, a 24-year-old might earn only about £14,500 a year—and is more likely to be on an unstable zero-hours contract, making budgeting and saving even harder.
